---
title: "How to plot region predictions along the probe"
---

A region decoder returns one row per channel. Drawn against depth, beside the histology,
those rows answer the question at a glance: where along the probe does the model agree with
the anatomy, where does it hesitate, and between which regions?

![The whole-probe decoder (ProbeTransformer, `2026_W42`) on the two probes bundled with it. For each probe, from left to right: the Cosmos regions from histology, the predicted region, and the full posterior as stacked bands. On `91fb4ed3` the prediction follows Isocortex, root and HPF but calls the bottom of the probe OLF. On `ea931b15` it finds Isocortex and midbrain (MB), while the hippocampus (HPF) between them shows up only as a minority band of the posterior.](../figures/predictions_along_probe.png){.lightbox}

The model and its example come from the Hugging Face Hub. The histology of the two example probes is open data in the
[IBL public database](https://docs.internationalbrainlab.org/public_docs/public_introduction.html),
read through [ONE](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/ONE/).

## Predict

The whole-probe decoder ships an example of two complete probes, with `axial_um`, so it can
be drawn along depth. (The XGBoost decoder's example is 500 channels drawn from many
probes, which cannot.)

```python
import pandas as pd
from ephysatlas import load_pretrained

model = load_pretrained(
    "int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-transformer", revision="2026_W42"
)
df = pd.read_parquet(model.path_model / "example" / "features_sample.parquet")
out = model.predict(df)
```

On your own probe, `df` is your aggregated and denoised table; see
[predict brain regions](../how-to/predict-regions.qmd).

## The histology to compare against

For an IBL insertion, the channel locations come with the spike sorting.
`SpikeSortingLoader.load_channels` returns them, with `axial_um` and an Allen `atlas_id`
per channel:

```python
from brainbox.io.one import SpikeSortingLoader
from one.api import ONE

one = ONE(base_url="https://openalyx.internationalbrainlab.org",
          password="international", silent=True)

pid = "91fb4ed3-ee27-4d7e-ba5d-f61202ed9884"
channels = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=pid, one=one).load_channels()
```

On your own recording, the histology is your traced track: the GUI's channel locations
after [alignment](../tutorials/where-is-my-probe.qmd#refine-with-histology), or any table
with `axial_um` and `atlas_id`.

## Plot

`figure_predictions_along_probe` draws one probe in three panels: the histology, the
predicted region and the class probabilities as stacked bands.

```python
import ephysatlas.plots

# The depth of each predicted channel: the decoder drops channels with non-finite features
pred = out.loc[pid].join(df.loc[pid, "axial_um"])

fig, axs = ephysatlas.plots.figure_predictions_along_probe(
    pred,
    pred["axial_um"],
    model.config["classes"],             # one id per class, in the order of the p_ columns
    histology=channels,                  # axial_um and an Allen atlas_id per channel
    mapping=model.config["region_map"],  # draw the histology in the model's Cosmos regions
    show_legend=True,
)
```

![The code above on probe `91fb4ed3`: the Cosmos regions from histology, the predicted region, and the probabilities of the 13 classes as stacked bands. The prediction follows Isocortex, root and HPF, and calls the bottom of the probe OLF.](../figures/predictions_one_probe.png){.lightbox}

The histology is mapped to the model's region map, so both bars use the same 13 classes.
The regions include the decoder's extra **`void_fluid`** class (id 2000), which plain
`iblatlas` `BrainRegions` does not know. If you pass your own `regions`, add that class
with `ClassifierRegions().add_new_region(NEW_VOID)` from `ephysatlas.anatomy`, or its band
is missing from the plot.

Each panel can be turned off (`show_histology`, `show_prediction`, `show_probabilities`),
and so can the acronyms on the bars (`show_labels`). To put several probes on one figure,
create the axes yourself and pass three per probe with `axs=`.
`examples/plot_predictions_along_probe.py` draws the figure at the top of this page that
way.

## Reading it

- **Where the bands are flat and one colour wins**, the model is sure. A long run of one
  predicted region against the same histology region is a confirmed stretch of probe.
- **Where two colours share the width**, the channel is ambiguous between them. These are
  usually neighbouring regions, and the boundary between them is where alignment errors
  hide. The runner-up is the second-largest band.
- **A region present in the histology but only as a thin band in the posterior** (HPF on
  `ea931b15`) is a region the decoder rarely gets right in isolation. The
  [confusion matrix](../how-to/predict-regions.qmd#predict-with-xgboost) says which.
- `prediction_probability` and `seed_agreement` (`fold_agreement` for the XGBoost decoder)
  are per-channel columns of `out`: plot them as two more strips to see the confidence
  along depth.

## In the alignment GUI

The [IBL alignment GUI](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/ibl-alignment-gui/) draws the same
predictions, live, beside the histology regions it is aligning. Its
[Channel Prediction plugin](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/ibl-alignment-gui/channel_prediction.html)
runs the decoders on an ibleatools feature table and lists them, with cumulative
versions, among the region plots.

For an IBL insertion, `ephysatlas.reveal.AtlasReveal` draws the decoder output beside the
features and the histology in one figure, `figure_02_classifier_results`. It needs ONE
access, and either your predictions (`df_predictions=`) or a local model directory
(`path_model=`).
